issues.description: The problem statement requires Farm to use a List implemented with an ArrayList for the animals attribute and to provide a getter and setter for that List. The provided solution instead defines the animals attribute as a Queue<Animal> and initializes it with a LinkedList, with getter/setter using Queue. This type mismatch between the specification and the solution (List/ArrayList vs Queue/LinkedList) is a structural inconsistency that could confuse students about the expected collection type and method signatures for the getter/setter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent with the problem statement: use List<Animal> as the field type and initialize it with new ArrayList<>() in the no-argument constructor, and change the getter/setter signatures to List<Animal>. Alternatively, if Queue semantics were intentional, update the problem statement and UML to specify Queue/LinkedList instead of List/ArrayList so all artifacts align.

issues.description: The problem statement requires the Farm to use a List implemented with an ArrayList for the animals aggregation, but the solution implements the animals collection as a Queue (LinkedList). This mismatch between the collection type named in the specification (List/ArrayList) and the concrete type used in the solution (Queue/LinkedList) can confuse students: they are instructed to initialize an ArrayList in the constructor but the provided final implementation uses a different interface and concrete class. Students may waste time reconciling the expected List/ArrayList with the solution's Queue/LinkedList and may implement the template incorrectly following the text instead of the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across artifacts. Either update the solution (and template) to use List<Animal> with new ArrayList<>() as the problem statement requests, or modify the problem statement to accept Queue/LinkedList as an allowed implementation. Preferably align to the problem text by changing the solution's field to 'private List<Animal> animals;' and initialize it with 'this.animals = new ArrayList<>();', updating imports accordingly.
